plan.title: Kidney treated-vs-control DE with PCA-structure audit
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human kidney bulk-RNA samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired) with raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 genes. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control, but the profiler flagged a real confound: PCA on these samples shows two clusters of six that do NOT follow condition. Because both the cluster split and the condition split are 6-vs-6, the two variables are either crossed (estimable together) or partially aligned — this must be quantified before any DE result is trusted. The plan therefore (1) verifies the count matrix, decides the correct DESeq2 input mode for Salmon-derived counts (integer counts vs corrected abundance, since the record does not say whether Salmon's length correction was applied), and characterizes the PCA structure explicitly — testing whether the 6/6 cluster is crossed with, aligned with, or independent of condition; (2) runs the primary DESeq2 analysis on ~condition and a pre-specified sensitivity analysis adding the data-driven cluster factor when the design matrix is full rank, reporting both models side by side rather than silently choosing one; (3) maps the DE result to WikiPathways human gene sets (provisioned, HGNC-symbol GMT matching this organism) via ranked-list GSEA and ORA; and (4) integrates everything into an honest report that states which genes are robust to the unknown structure and which are not. No batch variable exists in the metadata, so the cluster covariate is the only lever on the unwanted structure; the plan never treats it as a recorded batch.
